metadata.note: WEEKLY PROGRESS REEL for the loon-detector project (National Loon Center / 'Immer'), week of 2026-08-28. Eight-beat weekly-progress spine of WEEKLY-VIDEO-GUIDE.md. THE WEEK, as reported by the author, verbatim in scope: (1) both footage repositories and the git coding repository are initialized; (2) a guideline document was started on the ARCHITECTURE of the loon detection model, gathering the latest research and best practices; (3) the dataset is being prepared and image annotation has begun; (4) the project is at about 10%. THROUGH-LINE: nothing in a detector runs until the ground truth exists, so week one buys places, reasons and labels rather than model code. DOUBLE-CHECK LAW — THE ONLY FIGURE IN THIS REEL IS 10%, AND IT IS PROJECT-WIDE. The author was asked directly what the 10% measured and answered 'the whole project', so B04 and B05 say 'about ten percent of the project' and never 'ten percent of the images' or 'of the footage'. NO image counts, annotation counts, class counts, dataset sizes, accuracy or mAP figures appear anywhere — none were supplied. NO ARCHITECTURE IS NAMED. The author did not say which architectures the guideline document surveys, so B02 is built entirely around the ACT of choosing and recording, never around a candidate: no YOLO, no DETR, no R-CNN, no backbone, no framework. If a name is wanted on screen, the author must supply it. The 'two instances' on the B03 plate is a count of what is visible IN THAT ONE FRAME, not a dataset total. B04's claim that a labelling standard is cheaper to fix early is an EDITORIAL ARGUMENT the voice makes, not a report of a decision the author described. ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00, B06 and the verdict/outro only; the four body beats run ChipGrid -> BinaryBranch -> STILL -> DivergentFates, no two consecutive patterns repeated. SHORTS / 9:16: every Remotion pattern here has a registered *916 portrait sibling (ClaudeScienceChipGrid916, BinaryBranch916, DivergentFates916, ClaudeVerdictArtifact916, ClaudeComposerAsk916, ClaudeTitleOutro916), so shorts.py rewires the whole reel with no new TSX. B03 is user media and would otherwise be centre-cut, so it is covered by a hand-composed pantry/B03-916.png. NOTE: ScaleComparison was considered for B04 and REJECTED — its axis is log10 (Math.log10 in deckPatterns.tsx), built for orders-of-magnitude comparisons, and a 10% figure on a log axis is meaningless. typeScale 1.4 is set on the two deck patterns because they were authored against a 1280x720 stage; the *916 siblings take {data} only and ignore it harmlessly. At ~126s the reel is well under the 180s Shorts cap, so shorts.py reformats it whole with NO beats cut and NO outro rewrite. BRANDING RULE 7: slot-1 kicker stays 'Computational Skepticism'.

beats.narration_text: Nothing in a detector runs until somebody has told it what the thing looks like. This is Sai. This week was foundations, and none of it was model code. Three repositories initialized. A guideline document started on the architecture, written from the current research instead of from habit. And the first images annotated by hand.

beats.narration_text: Three repositories went up this week. Two for the footage, one for the code. That reads like housekeeping, and it isn't. A detector inherits whatever its dataset believes, so the order matters — the places first, then the reasons, then the labels. Model code is the last thing you write, not the first.

beats.narration_text: Then the document. The architecture for this detector is being chosen from the current research and the practices that actually hold up, and the choosing is being written down while it happens. That second part is the whole discipline. A model whose architecture you can't explain is a model you can't defend, and somebody will eventually ask.

beats.narration_text: And this is the actual work. Two loons on open water, two boxes drawn by hand. Look how much of this frame is not a loon. That's the real problem — the bird is a small dark shape on a surface that keeps moving, and every box like this one is a person deciding exactly where the bird ends and the lake begins.

beats.narration_text: The project is about ten percent in. That's small enough to feel like nothing, and it's exactly the moment that matters. Right now the labelling standard is still cheap to change. Every box drawn after it hardens gets drawn against a fixed line. Every box drawn before it is a box somebody may have to draw again.

beats.narration_text: So, week one. Three repositories, one architecture document, and the first images annotated. No model has been trained yet. That's the plan, not the delay — you don't get a second chance to decide what your ground truth means.

props.artifactHeading: Loon detector · week one, one page
artifactLines: Three repositories initialized — two for the footage, one for the code. Before anything is trained there is one known place for the raw material and one for the work that acts on it.

A guideline document started on the model architecture, drafted from the current research and the practices that hold up. The reasoning is being recorded as the choice is made, not reconstructed afterwards.
Dataset preparation underway, and the first images annotated by hand — boxes drawn one at a time on birds that are small, dark, and sitting on water that moves.
About ten percent of the project. No model has been trained yet, and at this stage that is the plan rather than the delay.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you're annotating anything right now, stop at the next hundred images and write your labelling rule down as instructions another person could follow. What counts as one instance. What you do with a half-hidden one. Where the box edge goes when the subject blurs into its background. Then ask which of those you'll regret.

props.command: I am ten percent into annotating a detection dataset. Before I go further, turn my labelling rule into something another person could follow — what counts as one instance, what to do with a partly hidden one, and where the box edge goes when the subject blurs into its background. Then tell me which of those decisions I am most likely to regret.

beats.narration_text: Ground truth first. The repositories, the document, and the first boxes drawn by hand. Next week, deeper into the annotation. Sai.
